ms.promise: A new open source project maintained by sundae labs. This project provides a binary that can be run, and read from the unix socket shared with the Hydra server, to consume the sequence of events, and produce a fascimile of the Ogmios API.
ms.criteria: The service provides at a minimum the v6 websocket APIs for chainsync and transaction submission; Any relevant data from the hydra head is passed through to the Ogmios API. Any details that don't make sense in a Hydra head are either stubbed out with sensible defaults, or return errors. We will evaluate the ledger state queries and mempool monitoring to decide if they make sense in the context of Hydra, and either implement, stub out, or error as appropriate. All this behavior is clearly documented.
ms.report:
This milestone delivers a plugin that reads from the Unix socket shared with the Hydra server and exposes APIs compatible with the Ogmios v6 WebSocket interface. The service enables chainsync and transaction submission functionality for Hydra heads, creating a seamless integration pathway for developers.
Acceptance Criteria
・The service implements v6 WebSocket APIs for chainsync and transaction submission.
・Relevant data from the Hydra head is passed through to the Ogmios API.
・Mempool queries were evaluated and deemed unnecessary, as Hydra signs snapshots immediately, making the concept of a mempool redundant due to near-instant transaction confirmation.
・Ledger state queries, including stake snapshots, were also evaluated and determined not to be applicable, as these features are not tracked or relevant within a Hydra head.

Evidence of Milestone Completion:
・GitHub Repository: https://github.com/SundaeSwap-finance/hydra-ogmios
・API Documentation: https://github.com/SundaeSwap-finance/hydra-ogmios/blob/main/README.md
・Video Demonstration: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JlDB0BwfkIw

ms.report:
Milestone 5: Solicit and implement feedback related to these two integrations
This milestone focused on gathering and implementing feedback from the developer community on the Hydra transaction streaming plugin. Our goal was to evaluate the developer experience and integration challenges related to the Hydra node extension, the Ogmios event server prototype, and Scrolls log source, and to improve the tooling and documentation accordingly.
Community Feedback Collection
We solicited public feedback through a Google Form distributed to the Cardano builder community. Three experienced contributors provided thoughtful insights:
・Sebastian Nagel (Ncōding)
・Juan Magan Valero (TxPipe)
・Matthias Benkort (Cardano Foundation / @KtorZ)

All three respondents confirmed the relevance of these tools to their workflows and shared suggestions such as:
・Expanding the documentation and examples for the EventSource and EventSink interfaces
・Improving modularity to support more flexible consumption of streamed data
・Interest in deeper Scrolls integration as a potential downstream consumer

The full responses are available here:
 https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1hAN6CEMMnRtuTirxXd6A68CBXFgOAb-ANvgvQ8t9Jms/edit?usp=sharing
Implementation
We authored user stories based on the collected feedback and implemented changes across the codebase. These changes focused on streamlining event handling, improving modularity, and publishing developer-facing documentation and examples.
Work related to this milestone is reflected in the following Hydra repository PRs and issues:
・https://github.com/cardano-scaling/hydra/pull/1000 – Initial groundwork
・https://github.com/cardano-scaling/hydra/pull/1348 – Event system refactor
・https://github.com/cardano-scaling/hydra/pull/1351 – Milestone 2 core logic
・https://github.com/cardano-scaling/hydra/issues/1618 – Use case for API server as event sink
・https://github.com/cardano-scaling/hydra/pull/1808 – Streamed events with constant memory
・https://github

ms.report:
We have completed the final milestone for the Hydra Transaction Stream Plugin project. This work delivers a pluggable event-stream architecture for the Hydra node, enabling developers to directly integrate Hydra transactions and events into their own tools and workflows without modifying Hydra’s core logic.
Key deliverables:
・Fully implemented plugin framework with documented EventSource and EventSink interfaces
・Real-world integrations including:
・Hydra Ogmios – Ogmios API served directly from a Hydra node over a binary unix socket
・Scrolls integration – Hydra event streams consumed by TxPipe’s Scrolls indexing framework
・S3 sink – Event persistence to Amazon S3 (adaptable for other blob storage)
・Architectural Decision Record (ADR) formalizing design principles and implementation approach
・Robust developer documentation and examples for extending the plugin
